How much is changing?
How we measure these signals
CURRENT VALUEAbove City = clearly above the group median; Around City = close to the median; Below City = clearly below it.
RECENT CHANGEGrowing Fast = strong recent increase; Growing = moderate increase; Stable = little change; Falling = decline.
TRANSIT ACCESSHigh = both metro and rail; Medium = one of the two. This is a simple category, not a 0–100 score.
CHANGE ON SITEHigh Change = many active local transformation signals; Active Change = some activity; Low Change = little current activity.
URBAN GREENSPOTTED mean green index for the relevant NIL. LOW / MID / HIGH are relative only to the five pilot areas, not a universal quality score.
AIR QUALITY / NO₂2024 annual NO₂ from the nearest active ARPA station. Lower NO₂ is better. This is a spatial proxy because five stations cannot measure every neighbourhood directly.
URBAN INTENSITYResidents per km². This describes how intensely the area is inhabited; it is not the same as building-footprint density.
LOCAL AMENITIES V1Schools per km². This is an education-only first layer; retail, food/leisure and personal services are explicitly reserved for the next expansion.
POPULATION TRENDGrowing = residents increasing; Stable = little change; Declining = residents decreasing.
MISSING DATAIf a value is unresolved, it stays unresolved. The interface does not invent missing values.
ENVIRONMENT DATA: Green = Comune di Milano / SPOTTED NIL Urban Green Index, July 2024. Air = 2024 annual NO₂ from the nearest active ARPA Milan station. Urban Intensity and Local Amenities V1 use Comune di Milano DS205; Amenities V1 is currently schools/km² only.

PROJECT / METHOD

About Atlas Milano.

CORE QUESTION
Can urban transformation be detected before it is reflected in property values?

ATLAS MILANO combines property values, urban signals, historical reconstruction and machine-learning validation to read how value and transformation move through Milan over time.

CURRENT V1 RESULTThe system can describe signals and test market patterns, but the evidence is not yet strong enough for a defensible neighbourhood price forecast. The app therefore shows transparent scenarios instead of pretending to know the future.
HOW TO USE THE APP
NEWSDiscover daily urban stories, filtered by theme and neighbourhood. Article links are not model observations.
MAPSee the current state of the five pilot areas.
HISTFollow reconstructed and observed value change over time.
SIGCompare current urban conditions one dimension at a time.
MLSee whether the forecasting models are reliable enough to trust.
SCNTest simple future “what if?” assumptions without calling them predictions.

DATA STATUS / LEGEND
OBSERVEDDirect value from an external source, such as OMI quotations or population data.
RESEARCH RECONSTRUCTIONHistorical estimate created for the pre-2004 period. It is descriptive, not transaction data.
CALCULATEDA value derived from observed data, such as annual change or value relative to the panel median.
MODELLEDA research indicator built from explicit rules, such as the current transformation signal.
SCENARIOA user-defined future assumption. It is not a model forecast.
LIMITS / NEXT VERSION

What V1 does not claim

It does not rank the “best” neighbourhood, provide an investment recommendation, estimate individual property prices or prove that one urban intervention causes value growth.

What V2 should add

More OMI–NIL mappings, richer public-transport accessibility, finer air-quality modelling, true building-footprint density, and a broader amenities layer covering retail, food/leisure and personal services.

RESEARCH LAB / THESIS PILOT

Behind the research.

Here we test whether changes in the city might reveal something about future property values. The evidence is still limited.
RESEARCH QUESTION
To what extent can open urban data detect neighbourhood transformation before such change is reflected in residential property values?
OBSERVED OMI PANEL38 ZONES
STRICT URBAN SAMPLE3 ZONES
URBAN PANEL27 ROWS
SIGNAL PERIOD2015–23
CASE STUDIES5 AREAS
CURRENT STATUS / PILOT ONLY. The app can demonstrate the research method, but the strict urban sample is too small for causal or statistically robust conclusions. The thesis question therefore remains open.
HYPOTHESES / CURRENT EVIDENCE
LEAD–LAG EXPLORER
Does a signal observed at year t relate to relative property growth over the following years?
METHOD: cumulative OMI price growth for each mapped area minus cumulative growth of the stable 38-zone median over the same horizon. The displayed coefficient is a within-area correlation after removing each area's average level. Positive means the signal and later relative growth move in the same direction; negative means they move in opposite directions.
DO NOT READ THIS AS CAUSATION. n = 27 / 24 / 21 observations but only 3 underlying areas. Repeated observations are not independent and no significance claim is made. This panel exists to test the thesis workflow before a larger database is obtained.
WHAT CAN BE TESTED TODAY?
POPULATION / MIGRATIONAnnual series available. Eligible for exploratory lag testing.
TRANSFORMATIONTime-varying selected-event signal available, but still hand-curated.
URBAN INTENSITYAnnual population density available.
SCHOOL DENSITYAnnual series available, but it is only a partial amenities proxy.
TRANSIT ACCESSNot testable temporally in the strict sample because V1 is constant within each mapped area.
GREEN + AIR2024 snapshot only. Useful in Signals, not yet eligible for historical lead–lag testing.
THESIS DATA GATE
The next database should turn the current demonstration into a defensible empirical study.
CURRENT3strict zones
MINIMUM GATE8+mapped zones
THESIS TARGET30+mapped zones
Priority data: annual amenities by category; travel-time accessibility; project announcement/start/completion dates and scale; yearly green/environment series; more defensible OMI↔NIL mappings.
CURRENT RESEARCH CONCLUSION
The present dataset is sufficient to prototype the method, but not to answer the thesis question conclusively.

That is not a failure condition. It establishes the first empirical baseline, reveals which variables need better temporal coverage, and defines exactly what a new university or commercial database must contain before ATLAS MILANO can make stronger claims.

SIMPLE RULE TO BEATSAME AS THE MARKETA model must beat the simple rule that each area moves with the wider market.
BEST NON-ML ALTERNATIVE4.24% MAEZone Historical Mean — still worse than the 3.93% simple benchmark.
BEST ML MODEL4.46% MAEXGBoost — useful for testing, but not reliable enough for a public point forecast.
Reliability checkNO-GOAll five critical reliability criteria are not passed.
IMPORTANT LIMITATION / URBAN DATA
The current 38-area predictive model relies mainly on market, macro and zone-identity variables. Demography, transit access and change-on-site variables exist, but only 3 strictly mapped zones / 27 rows are available — too little for a strong ML claim about urban effects.

Next step: expand the mapped zones and add richer access, green-space, urban-fabric and amenity data.

ATLAS MILANO is the Milan research prototype developed within Urban Intelligence, reading the relationship between urban change and property value.
